co_mt_blue_sky_formerly_mount_evans_mixe.approach: The start is beside the upper Snave couloir, on its left. With a vehicle at the top, drive up to the summit lot, walk the trail walk the trail to the little notch under the summit, then traverse the angled snow band toward the northeast to reach the base. A narrow snow tongue runs up to an iced corner roofed by a flake, which you pass by tunnelling beneath it. The summit road (Highway 5) is seasonal and closed in winter, so in the cold months the approach adds a long walk up the road or in from Echo Lake via the Chicago Lakes basin. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

From the Summit Lake parking area, take the broad trail toward the notch that faces the Tan Buttresses, then drop down and left into the cirque and continue down to the foot of the nearest buttress. Several gullies lead toward the ridge; this one has a prominent right-facing fin forming its upper gully, just left of Snorkmaiden's Surprise. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

The summit road (Highway 5) is seasonal and closed in winter, so in the cold months the approach adds a long walk up the road or in from Echo Lake via the Chicago Lakes basin. From the Summit Lake parking area, follow the wide trail toward the notch opposite the Tan Buttresses, then descend leftward into the cirque to the foot of the nearest buttress. Several gullies lead toward the ridge; this is the rightmost of them, just right of the Micro Goulotte. The two routes merge after the start into a moderate snow gully with mixed steps leading to the ridgeline. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

co_mt_blue_sky_formerly_mount_evans_mixe.descent_text: The gully finishes by topping out on the hiker's trail that leads toward Mt. Spaulding. Follow that trail back along the rim to the Chicago Lakes overlook, a short walk from the Summit Lake area. Take care on the narrow upper gully and on any cornice or soft snow at the exit. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

co_mt_blue_sky_formerly_mount_evans_mixe.approach: This climb is on the true north face and is entered from above. Drive to the summit, then rappel from the true summit (the highest point, with the USGS marker) down onto a snow-covered ramp below the climb. Wear a helmet, since the face is loose in places and gets no sun. The summit road (Highway 5) is seasonal and closed in winter, so in the cold months the approach adds a long walk up the road or in from Echo Lake via the Chicago Lakes basin. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
